blog.title: My static site got a tool loop — and maybe an agent
blog.description: I wanted my chat assistant to answer a question about a real Bundestag session. Here is everything that has to happen between the question and the answer — and why all of it runs in your browser.

nftMetadata.description:
AI generated artwork based on the prompt: "A highly detailed digital illustration of a browser as a puppeteer controlling three marionettes, each representing a tool in a technical workflow. The scene is set on a dark, gradient stage with a circuit-board floor that glows faintly with hex values and binary code. The puppeteer is a translucent, wireframe hand emerging from the left side of the frame, holding thin, glowing strings like marionette strings. The strings connect to three distinct marionettes floating in mid-air:

1. **Mistral LLM Endpoint Marionette:** An abstract figure with a hexagonal head made of swirling JSON text and a body composed of curly braces and code snippets. Its strings attach to its head and "hands" (shaped like { }). The color scheme is deep blue and purple, with glowing accents.

2. **Bundestakt API Marionette:** A minimalist, geometric figure with a head shaped like the German flag or the Bundestag logo. Its body resembles a database table or stack of documents, with black, red, and gold colors and white highlights.

3. **Image Generator Marionette:** A whimsical, painterly figure with a head shaped like a palette and brush. Its body is made of abstract pixels and shapes, with warm pastel colors (pink, teal, yellow).

The strings are thin, glowing lines (like fiber optics or neon) with small data packets traveling along them, labeled with terms like "GET," "POST," "JSON," and "tool_calls." The background features faint outlines of a browser window and server racks, blurred to keep focus on the marionettes. The style is semi-realistic with a touch of surrealism, dramatic lighting, and a mix of smooth digital surfaces and handcrafted textures."

prevBlog.title: How quantum circuits can mitigate the tragedy of the commons
prevBlog.description: I explore whether a quantum circuit can generate the institution that keeps two islands from overfishing the ground they share — what the entanglement changes, what it recovers from economics, and what it leaves untouched.

nftMetadata.description: AI generated artwork based on the prompt: "A sophisticated conceptual illustration of two small islands sharing one common fishing ground. Each island has its own small fleet of fishing boats, initially heading independently toward the same rich patch of ocean. Beneath and between the islands, the water subtly transforms into an elegant abstract quantum circuit: two parallel paths representing the two players become coupled through a beautiful symmetric entangling structure, then separate again toward the islands. The quantum circuit should feel like an invisible mechanism underneath the physical world, not a literal computer. Show the shared resource and the coupling between the players as the central visual idea. Clean, spacious, intellectually curious, realistic landscape combined with restrained scientific abstraction, deep ocean, crisp geometry, no text, no labels, no equations, no futuristic clichés, no glowing blue sci-fi computer, editorial scientific illustration, calm and understated, visually explaining an economic mechanism rather than decorating it."
